settings.heading: Density isn't firmness.
settings.body:
Density is the weight of a cubic metre of foam. It is not the same thing as firmness, which is why a cheap bed can feel reassuringly solid in the shop and still be flat by March. Firmness is how it feels on day one. Density is how much foam is in there to keep feeling that way.

A lot of dog beds are filled with shredded offcuts or low-density foam, and those can bottom out inside a year, at which point your dog is sleeping on the floor with a cover over it. Our orthopaedic cores are 50kg/m³, which is the reason the guarantee is on the foam rather than on the stitching.

This is how the orthopaedic beds are built. The fibre-filled nest beds are made differently, and we say so on the page rather than letting you find out in month three.

settings.heading: Why they are named after fells and dales.
settings.body:
Borrowdale, Coniston, Grasmere, Windermere. The range takes its names from the places the walking gets done at weekends, which is also where most of the thinking about these beds happened.

Each one is built around a sleeping style rather than a price point. Curlers get walls. Sprawlers get surface. Old joints get foam that does not bottom out. Where a bed is fibre-filled rather than foam, the product page says so.
settings.places: Borrowdale, Coniston, Grasmere, Windermere, Kendal, Ambleside

settings.question: How do I know which size to get?
settings.answer: Measure nose to base of tail while they are lying down, then add 15–20cm. Where a dog falls between two sizes, go up: sprawlers need the length more than you would think. Every product page has a size guide built from that bed's own measurements, with breed examples.

settings.question: What does 50kg/m³ actually mean? Isn't firmer better?
settings.answer:
It is how much foam is packed into every cubic metre. Density and firmness are not the same thing: a low-density foam can feel firm on day one and still collapse by month six. High-density foam keeps its structure under repeated weight, which is why a 50kg/m³ core is still supporting hips and elbows years later.

You'll find it in the orthopaedic beds. The fibre-filled nest beds are built for softness instead, and each product page says which is which.

settings.question: Can I actually wash it?
settings.answer:
On most of the range, yes: properly, not just spot-clean. Covers zip off and go straight in the machine at 30°C, and on the orthopaedic beds a waterproof inner liner keeps wet coats, muddy paws and accidents away from the foam.

One exception worth knowing before you buy: waterproof-fabric beds are wiped clean rather than washed with detergent, because detergent strips the coating off the fabric. Every product page says which applies.

settings.question: How quickly will it arrive?
settings.answer: Orders go out on working days, tracked from the moment they leave us. Order by [cutoff] on a dispatch day and it goes the same day; most then arrive within [delivery_min]–[delivery_max] working days. Tracking comes by email as soon as it's on its way.

settings.question: What does delivery cost?
settings.answer: Delivery is free on UK orders over [threshold]. Below that, the delivery charge is shown at checkout before you pay, so you always see it before you commit.

settings.question: What if my dog just won't use it?
settings.answer: Then it comes back. Let your dog sleep on it for up to [trial_nights] nights. [trial_terms] Just tell us inside that window. It doesn't need to be unused: send it back slept-on, hair and all. Full terms are in our [returns_policy].

settings.question: What does the [guarantee_years]-year guarantee cover?
settings.answer: The foam. Every memory foam bed carries a [guarantee_years]-year guarantee on its core: if it loses its structure under normal use in that time, which is the failure that ends most dog beds, we'll replace it. Covers, zips and liners are wearing parts and sit outside it, and the fibre-filled nest beds are built for softness rather than covered by the foam guarantee. Full terms are in our [returns_policy].

settings.question: Will it help a dog with arthritis or stiff hips?
settings.answer: A supportive bed spreads their weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders, which is what makes lying down and getting back up harder for a dog with joint wear. But a bed is not a treatment and it won't replace veterinary care, so please keep talking to your vet. What it can change is the surface they spend twelve to fourteen hours a day on.
